scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Count work before claiming speed
scenes.caption: Kabir compares synthetic record collections of eight, sixteen and thirty two items. He counts record probes and pair comparisons rather than using a stopwatch. Different assumptions can change what a count means.
scenes.dialogue: What is one unit of work here?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Four patterns of growth
scenes.caption: A known-position indexed read takes one counted access. A last-item linear search visits every record. A sorted binary search narrows the interval. Comparing every unordered pair grows much faster as the input increases.
scenes.dialogue: A low count needs its preparation assumptions.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Read the counted table
scenes.caption: For eight, sixteen and thirty two records, last-item linear search needs eight, sixteen and thirty two probes. The supplied sorted binary trace needs four, five and six. All-pairs comparisons number twenty eight, one hundred twenty and four hundred ninety six.
scenes.dialogue: The exact counts support a qualitative growth explanation.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the valid assumption
scenes.caption: Can binary search discard half an arbitrary shuffled list, or must sorted order be established first? Choose the statement that also keeps sorting and index-building effort visible.
scenes.dialogue: An algorithm depends on its preconditions.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A bounded efficiency claim
scenes.caption: Kabir describes constant, logarithmic, linear and quadratic growth for these counted operations. Big O concerns how work grows under stated assumptions; it is not a promise of elapsed time or a substitute for correctness.
scenes.dialogue: A fast wrong result is still wrong.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the growth lab
scenes.caption: Build the three-size operation table, inspect exact counts and explain the ordering and preparation limits. The classroom counter is bounded and does not benchmark a real service.
scenes.dialogue: Count the work you actually claim to compare.
